## Description
Makes kill-me's **pre-merge** CI (`docker-build-check.yaml`) publish a runnable image tagged by the **full commit SHA** to ACR, so the test-slot **deploy-to-image** flow can resolve a *verified, not-yet-merged* commit to its CI-built image.

Today the pre-merge check is build-only (`push: false`) and the only ACR push happens post-merge in `build-and-deploy.yaml` (tagging the short-7 SHA). That means an unmerged commit has no image, so deploy-to-image cannot deploy verified-but-unmerged work. This adopts pre-merge SHA-tagged image publishing for an app that lacked it, per the project owner's approval to roll this out to apps without pre-merge builds.

Sibling pattern: tank-operator #1256 (the pre-merge image-build adoption used as the reference), part of the test-slot deploy-to-image migration (Stage 5 — per-app CI publishes a SHA-resolvable image).

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Infrastructure change
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactor

## Changes Made
- `permissions:` add `id-token: write` (alongside `contents: read`) for `azure/login` OIDC.
- Add **Azure Login (OIDC)** and **ACR login** steps, reusing build-and-deploy.yaml's exact wiring:
  - `azure/login@v3` with `client-id: ${{ vars.ARM_CLIENT_ID }}`, `tenant-id: ${{ vars.ARM_TENANT_ID }}`, `subscription-id: ${{ vars.ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}` (GitHub **vars**, OIDC — no new secrets).
  - `az acr login --name romainecr`.
- Convert the single existing `docker/build-push-action@v7` step from `push: false` to a gated push of `romainecr.azurecr.io/kill-me:${{ github.sha }}` — the **full** `github.sha` (not the short-7 form used post-merge), because the deploy-to-image resolver resolves `git_ref` to the full SHA. Same Dockerfile/context (`context: .`, `file: Dockerfile`) build-and-deploy uses. No image matrix (single webapp).
- The login steps and the build step's `push:` are gated on:
  `github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`
  so the push happens on same-repo PRs and `workflow_dispatch`, and **fork PRs stay build-only** (no OIDC, no ACR login, `push: false`).
- For `workflow_dispatch` with a `git_ref`, the existing resolver now also sets `IMAGE_TAG` to the resolved full SHA, so the image is tagged with the exact requested commit (what deploy-to-image looks up) rather than the dispatch ref's HEAD.

## Testing
- [ ] Tested locally
- [x] Workflow passes
- [ ] Deployment verified

<sub>Opening this same-repo PR triggers the modified `docker-build-check` run, which will perform the first real Azure/ACR login + push of `romainecr.azurecr.io/kill-me:<full PR head SHA>`. The build itself is unchanged (same Dockerfile/context), so the build path is already exercised by the prior build-only check. Deploy-to-image consumption is validated separately in the deploy-to-image work.</sub>

## Checklist
- [x] Code follows project style guidelines
- [x] Self-reviewed the code
- [x] Updated documentation if needed
- [x] No breaking changes (or documented if necessary)

## Related Issues
- Test-slot **deploy-to-image** migration, Stage 5 (per-app CI publishes a SHA-resolvable image).
- Sibling pre-merge image-build pattern: tank-operator #1256.

## Deployment Notes
- No production deploy behavior changes. `build-and-deploy.yaml` (post-merge) is untouched and still owns the short-7-SHA production tag + kustomization bump.
- This only adds a pre-merge ACR push of the **full-SHA** tag for trusted (non-fork) events. The full SHA and short-7 SHA are different tags, so there is no collision with production tags.
- Requires the repo to already expose `ARM_CLIENT_ID` / `ARM_TENANT_ID` / `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` GitHub Actions **variables** and an OIDC federated-credential trust for this repo — both already used by `build-and-deploy.yaml`, so no new credential setup is needed.
